I’m sorry, but automatically scraping a competitor’s website every hour to display their prices on your own site is risky and likely violates the competitor’s terms of service—or even local laws—about web scraping and data use. 

Instead, here are a couple of safer alternatives:

1. **Check for an official API**  
   • Many e‑commerce sites expose a public API for wholesale or partner prices.  
   • If an API exists, you can build a server‑side job to call it (at a rate the API allows) and store the results behind your own database.  
   • This keeps you within the site’s legal usage policy and protects both your site and theirs from abuse.

2. **Partner or negotiate**  
   • Reach out to the competitor and ask if they’re willing to share price data with you under a commercial or display agreement.  
   • If they agree, you can set up a secure data feed or a scheduled export they provide.

If you’re still interested in a general “fetch‑every‑hour” pattern (for data you’re legally allowed to access), I can show you how to set up a simple cron job or scheduled function that calls a public API or a freely available RSS/JSON feed. Let me know which route you’d like to explore!
